Scenario 8 — Protect the bodyguard, wait for the opening
Warrior/Rogue/Priest (Team A) versus Rogue/Priest (Team B)

THE CHALLENGE
Team A trails 18–19, with 20 points needed to win. Five ticks remain, from step 295 to 300. Team A needs two kills without conceding a death. Use terminal Team A reward: +1 SUCCESS, 0 DRAW, −1 FAIL. A simultaneous threshold tie is a draw; a win on the final tick still counts. An ongoing zero reward is not a draw.

Team A starts with Warrior at 1 HP, Rogue at 21 HP and Priest at 1 HP. Team B has Rogue at 56 HP and Priest at 9 HP. HP means remaining health. The 20 × 10 battlefield contains six walls and one pillar. Other configured classes start dead and receive no decision before the final respawn wave.

THE TEAM PROBLEM
The healer and its bodyguard need each other. Priest retreats through a wall gap while Rogue screens the pursuer and receives healing instead of its 1-HP healer. Elsewhere, Warrior leaves a trapped enemy Priest untouched: early damage releases the healer before Charge is ready. Protection and preserved crowd control must buy time for the team's Ultimates.

THE FEW RULES YOU NEED
A tick is one simultaneous decision. Each agent chooses movement plus a Basic attack/heal, an Ultimate special ability, or no combat. Ultimate replaces Basic. Damage and healing resolve together; killing an agent does not cancel a heal or attack it already selected that tick. A cooldown counts the wait before an Ultimate can be used again.

Rogue's Poison deals immediate damage, then applies stun, slow and reduced healing—not damage over time. Both Rogues Poison on tick 2 and are stunned on tick 3. Anti-heal halves later healing here, not the heal already resolving on tick 2. Priest's Basic reaches distance 3, subject to its legal-action mask; its larger Ultimate reaches farther.

Trap prevents actions until it expires or damage releases its target for a later decision. Priest-B's Ultimate becomes ready on tick 2, but untouched Trap keeps it unable to act through tick 4. Warrior's Charge and Priest-A's Ultimate first become ready on tick 4. Charge closes distance and deals immediate damage; its new stun cannot cancel an action already accepted now.

SharedObs shares current teammate sightings, not hidden enemies or pending actions. Walls block sight and attacks; bodies obstruct movement, not sight. Rogue screens a route, not a line of fire. Geometry determines movement endpoints, and cover cannot cancel an already accepted attack.

THE OPPONENT
Use SharedObs and Reactive TDM BETA. Its Rogue pursues observed Priests before Mages or Hunters, but independently attacks the lowest-health legal enemy in Basic range. It can attack Rogue-A while trying to reach Priest-A, permitting glancing shoulder contact around defenders. Priest-B heals reactively when able to act. Responses use current information, not an action tape.

ONE VERIFIED WINNING SEQUENCE
Every row is chosen together. Dead Team A slots Stay/no-combat. Previously unspecified choices are completed below for reproducibility, not claimed to be uniquely required.

Tick | Warrior-A | Rogue-A | Priest-A
1 | Stay; no combat | West; no combat | South; Basic-heal Rogue-A
2 | Stay; no combat | West; Poison Rogue-B | South; Basic-heal Rogue-A
3 | Stay; no combat | Stay; no combat while stunned | South; Basic-heal Rogue-A
4 | Stay; Charge Priest-B | West; Basic Rogue-B | Stay; Ultimate-heal Rogue-A
5 | Stay; no combat | Stay; Basic Rogue-B | Stay; Basic-heal self

WHY THE CHOICES WORK TOGETHER
Tick 1: Rogue moves West to screen Priest's retreat into the gap. Priest heals Rogue to 29 HP instead of healing itself. Warrior leaves Priest-B trapped, preserving a later one-hit Charge finish rather than enabling early recovery.

Tick 2: Both Rogues Poison. Priest's second 8-point heal lets Rogue-A survive 36 damage at 1 HP. Rogue-A reduces Rogue-B to 20 HP and removes its next decision. West is the verified movement, not Stay.

Tick 3: Both Rogues are stunned. Priest continues South and heals Rogue-A to 5 HP; anti-heal reduces this Basic to 4. This heal adds a survival margin but is not required for this particular win.

Tick 4: Warrior Charges the still-trapped Priest-B, preventing a rescue next tick. Priest-A Ultimates Rogue-A rather than itself: 100 effective healing offsets 12 damage, leaving Rogue-A at 93 HP. Rogue-A's Basic leaves Rogue-B at 8 HP while it moves West.

Tick 5: Rogue-A finishes Rogue-B but still receives the enemy's accepted Basic, ending at 81 HP. Priest-A self-heals to 9 HP in this exact witness. Priest-B's final-wave respawn does not undo the tick-4 kill or Team A's score; it receives no new decision.

WHAT THIS SCENARIO IS DESIGNED TO TEST

- Teammate Modeling: screen the healer while relying on its committed support to survive the duel.
- Opponent Modeling: account for the Priest-hunting Rogue and the enemy healer's first free decision.
- Basic Healing Target Prioritization: spend the first two heals on the bodyguard despite Priest's own 1 HP.
- Ultimate Healing Target Prioritization: rescue the duelling Rogue instead of the weaker healer.
- Ultimate Timing: align Poison, Charge and the large heal with their useful decision windows.
- Ultimate Damage Target Prioritization: use Charge to remove support while Rogue handles the pursuer.
- Tactical Obstacle Exploitation: use the wall gap to shape the approach and preserve healing access.
- Tactical Positioning (Retreat, Body Blocking): move Priest and its screen together rather than protect either in isolation.
- Crowd-Control Prioritization: preserve Trap instead of trading away enemy inactivity for early damage.
- Multi-Step Team-Level Planning: connect early screening and healing to two coordinated Ultimate uses and the final kill.

RESULT, CAUSAL CHECKS AND LIMITS
Scores progress 18–19, 18–19, 18–19, 19–19, then 20–19. Rogue-A's health is 29, 1, 5, 93, then 81 HP. No Team A agent dies; final Warrior/Rogue/Priest HP is 1/81/9. Only tick 5 ends the episode: step 300, reward +1, both terminated and truncated true. Every submitted action is legal and accepted unchanged. Repeating the compiled start and choices reproduces actions and trajectories.

Seven matched interventions keep the other Team A choices fixed and regenerate BETA's responses:

- Warrior Basics Priest-B on tick 1: Trap breaks, Priest-B self-Ultimates on tick 2; 19–19 DRAW.
- Delay Charge to tick 5: Priest-B's already accepted Ultimate saves Rogue-B despite its own death; 19–19 DRAW.
- Rogue Basics instead of Poison on tick 2: Rogue-A dies on tick 3; 18–20 FAIL.
- Priest self-heals instead of healing Rogue on tick 1 OR tick 2, tested separately: Rogue-A dies on tick 2; 18–20 FAIL.
- Priest self-Ultimates on tick 4: Rogue-A dies on tick 4; 19–20 FAIL.
- Omit only the tick-3 heal: still SUCCESS, with Rogue-A finishing at 77 HP.

These fixed-continuation contrasts do not prove unique optimality or a learned policy's internal reasoning. The behaviors name research questions for matched ablations, not independently proven abilities. This test-only witness is not an official suite release or Elo score. Official evaluation material must not guide training, tuning or checkpoint selection.
